questions.question: Buffeting is the intermittent application of forces to part of an airplane. It is caused by:
questions.explanation: Buffeting is caused by unsteady airflow, including turbulence, that produces fluctuating aerodynamic forces.

questions.question: With which system is differential control associated?
questions.explanation: Differential ailerons use unequal upward and downward deflection to reduce adverse yaw.

questions.question: The purpose of spring tabs or servo tabs is to:
choices: Assist the pilot in moving the control surfaces
Contribute to the static balance of the control surface
questions.answerText: Assist the pilot in moving the control surfaces
questions.explanation: A spring or servo tab helps move the primary control surface, reducing the force the pilot must apply.

questions.question: The purpose of the vertical fin is to provide:
questions.explanation: The vertical fin resists sideslip and provides directional stability about the vertical axis.

questions.question: If the control stick of an aircraft with properly rigged flight controls is moved rearward and to the left, the right aileron will move:
choices: Down and the elevator will move down
Up and the elevator will move down
Down and the elevator will move up
Up and the elevator will move up
questions.answerText: Down and the elevator will move up
questions.explanation: Aft stick moves the elevator up. Left stick raises the left aileron and lowers the right aileron.

questions.question: Which statement about the difference between Krueger flaps and slats is correct?
choices: A Krueger flap forms a slot; a slat does not
A slat increases critical angle of attack; a Krueger flap does not
A Krueger flap increases critical angle of attack; a slat does not
A slat forms a slot; a Krueger flap does not
questions.answerText: A slat forms a slot; a Krueger flap does not
questions.explanation: A deployed slat creates a slot that energizes the flow over the upper wing surface. A Krueger flap does not form that slot.

questions.question: What is the most effective flap system?
questions.explanation: A Fowler flap increases both wing camber and effective wing area, producing a large lift increase.

questions.question: On an aircraft, the Krueger flap is a:
choices: Leading-edge flap close to the wing root
Leading-edge flap close to the wing tip
questions.answerText: Leading-edge flap close to the wing root
questions.explanation: A Krueger flap is a leading-edge device commonly installed near the wing root.

questions.question: Where does the lift act on the wing?
choices: Always forward of the centre of gravity
questions.explanation: The resultant aerodynamic lift acts through the centre of pressure for the current flight condition.

questions.question: The lateral axis is also called the:
questions.explanation: The lateral axis runs from wingtip to wingtip and is the pitch axis.

questions.question: Pitch angle is defined as:
choices: The angle between the chord line and the free-stream flow velocity
The angle between the chord line and the relative airflow
The angle between the aircraft longitudinal axis and the local horizon
The angle between the lower wing surface and the relative airflow
questions.answerText: The angle between the aircraft longitudinal axis and the local horizon
questions.explanation: Pitch attitude is measured between the aircraft longitudinal axis and the local horizon.

questions.question: When the stick is moved forward, the stabilizer lift:
questions.explanation: Moving the stick forward commands a nose-down change; the resulting tail force changes to provide the required pitching moment.

questions.question: In straight and level flight, the centre of pressure is behind the centre of gravity. With the resultant force from the elevators and tailplane action to maintain straight and level flight, the force would be:
choices: In a direction depending on the thrust/drag couple
questions.explanation: With the centre of pressure aft of the centre of gravity, a downward tail force supplies the balancing nose-up moment.

questions.question: If an aircraft is pitching up:
choices: The incidence angle first increases and then decreases
questions.explanation: The angle of incidence is a fixed geometric angle between the chord line and the aircraft longitudinal axis; pitching does not change it.

questions.question: Which is the correct description of the method for measuring the dihedral angle?
choices: The angle between the wing plane and the horizontal
The angle between a line through the 25% wing chord and the horizontal axis
The angle between the 25% chord and the lateral axis
The angle between the 25% chord line and the horizontal axis
questions.answerText: The angle between the wing plane and the horizontal
questions.explanation: Dihedral is the angle between the wing plane and the horizontal reference plane.

questions.question: Longitudinal dihedral is:
choices: The difference between the wing and tail dihedral angles
The difference between the wing and tail angles of incidence
When the wing has anhedral and the tail dihedral
The difference between the wing and tail angles of sweep
questions.answerText: The difference between the wing and tail angles of incidence
questions.explanation: Longitudinal dihedral is the difference between the wing and tailplane incidence angles.

questions.question: If an increase in power tends to make the nose of the aircraft dip, this is the result of the:
choices: Centre of lift being ahead of the centre of gravity
Centre of lift and centre of gravity being collocated
Line of thrust being above the centre of gravity
Line of thrust passing through the centre of gravity
questions.answerText: Line of thrust being above the centre of gravity
questions.explanation: A thrust line above the centre of gravity creates a nose-down pitching moment when thrust increases.

questions.question: The angle between the aeroplane longitudinal axis and the chord line is the:
questions.explanation: Angle of incidence is the fixed angle between the aircraft longitudinal axis and the wing chord line.

questions.question: How is longitudinal stability affected by positive camber of the aerofoil?
choices: Positive, because the centre of pressure shifts rearward as angle of attack increases
Negative, because the lift vector rotates forward as angle of attack increases
Positive, because the lift vector rotates backward as angle of attack increases
No effect, because camber produces a constant pitch-down moment coefficient independent of angle of attack
questions.answerText: No effect, because camber produces a constant pitch-down moment coefficient independent of angle of attack
questions.explanation: The source key identifies the constant pitch-down moment coefficient of a cambered aerofoil as producing no change in longitudinal stability with angle of attack.

questions.question: Which aeroplane behaviour will be corrected by a yaw damper?
questions.explanation: A yaw damper senses and counters yaw oscillations, damping Dutch roll.

questions.question: The aft movement of the centre of pressure during acceleration through the transonic flight regime will:
questions.explanation: An aft shift of the centre of pressure increases the longitudinal stability contribution in the condition described.

questions.question: Flap selection at constant IAS in straight and level flight will increase the:
questions.explanation: Extending flaps raises maximum lift coefficient and increases drag.

questions.question: When spoilers are used as speed brakes:
choices: CLmax of the polar curve is not affected
They do not affect wheel-braking action during landing
At the same angle of attack, CL remains unaffected
At the same angle of attack, CD is increased and CL is decreased
questions.answerText: At the same angle of attack, CD is increased and CL is decreased
questions.explanation: Spoilers add drag and disrupt lift, increasing CD while decreasing CL at the same angle of attack.

questions.question: After a disturbance about the lateral axis, an aeroplane oscillates about the lateral axis at a constant amplitude. The aeroplane is:
questions.explanation: A restoring response indicates static stability. Constant oscillation amplitude indicates neutral dynamic stability.

questions.question: What increases the stalling angle of attack? Use of:
questions.explanation: Slats delay flow separation and let the wing reach a higher angle of attack before stalling.

questions.question: Which of the following are used as stall-warning devices?
questions.explanation: A stick shaker warns the pilot through the controls; a stall strip can trigger the aerodynamic warning cues used by the source material.

questions.question: When power-assisted controls are used for pitch control, this:
choices: Makes aerodynamic balancing of the control surfaces meaningless
Can function only with an elevator trim tab
Ensures that part of the aerodynamic forces is still felt on the column
questions.answerText: Ensures that part of the aerodynamic forces is still felt on the column
questions.explanation: The control system is arranged so the pilot retains aerodynamic feedback through the column.

questions.question: A plain flap will increase CLmax by:
choices: Increasing the camber of the aerofoil
questions.answerText: Increasing the camber of the aerofoil
questions.explanation: A plain flap increases aerofoil camber, raising the maximum lift coefficient.

questions.question: A horn balance in a control system has the following purpose:
choices: Decrease the effective longitudinal dihedral of the aeroplane
questions.explanation: A horn balance reduces hinge moment and therefore lowers the pilot force needed to move the control surface.

questions.question: Winglets:
questions.explanation: Winglets reduce wingtip-vortex losses and induced drag.
